title: Proactive watermark-based prober for VPC upgrade and throughput regressions
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: During private (VPC) runtime upgrades we have seen subtle throughput and tail-latency regressions that escape coarse probes. Existing synthetic probes typically exercise steady-state load and miss short-duration saturation events and token-level regressions that impact multi-tenant customers.

Goal: Implement a proactive, watermark-driven probing system that detects imminent token throughput saturation and latency regressions during upgrades and routine health checks. The prober should operate at multiple granularities: per-tenant, per-route, and per-worker. It must plug into our Terraform/IaC modules so canary and baseline probes are provisioned and pinned automatically during upgrade rollouts.

Key ideas: 1) Watermark probes emit short bursts of token-heavy synthetic traffic with increasing token-rate envelopes (e.g., 50th/90th/99th watermark levels) and measure token-acceptance rate, kv-cache hit ratio, and p99 generation latency. 2) Adaptive thresholds are computed by comparing current rollout candidate to a rolling baseline derived from the target environment's recent telemetry (7d window). 3) Probe shepherding hooks are exposed in the Terraform module: probe version pin, probe schedule, canary scope selection, and automated fail-fast flags for rollback. 4) Export metrics via Prometheus/OpenTelemetry with labels for tenant_id, route, rollout_id, and probe_seed so downstream alerting and SLO dashboards can create dynamic windows.

Success criteria: reliable early detection of degradation patterns that previously required manual diagnosis (e.g., soft token rejections, KV cache thrash). Minimize false positives by using relative-watermark comparisons and ensemble signals (error-rate + token-acceptance slope + latency quantiles).

Operational constraints: low resource footprint for probes (synthetic burst <= 2% of node capacity), non-disruptive to customer traffic, and clear IaC lifecycle so probes are created/removed with each canary.

Design notes: - Probe types: ramping-burst, sustained-window, and quiescent-check. - Metrics tracked: token_accept_rate, token_rejects, gen_latency_p50/p90/p99, kv_cache_hit_ratio, out_of_capacity_errors, cpu_util_percent, gpu_mem_pressure. - Adaptive decision logic: compute z-score of candidate vs baseline for each metric; fail if ensemble score > threshold for X consecutive windows. - Integration points: terraform/modules/vpc-probes (new), console rollouts API, alertmanager rules repo, and the canary operator.

Terraform integration: - Add a probes submodule with resources: probe_config (versioned), probe_scheduler (cron/cadence), iam roles, and provisioning hooks tied to canary resources. - probe_config includes: probe_image, token_rate_profile, target_routes, tenant_selector, alert_thresholds_ref. - Expose var.probe_enable, var.probe_policy (fail_fast | warn_only), and var.probe_version for pinning.

Documentation: Confluence doc will be created under "Private Deploy Health / Watermark Probes" with runbook snippets and sample Terraform usage.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module 'vpc-probes' creates probe resources when var.probe_enable=true and can be pinned with var.probe_version
Probes emit labeled Prometheus/OpenTelemetry metrics for token_accept_rate, gen_latency_p99, and kv_cache_hit_ratio
Console UI shows probe rollouts with baseline vs candidate comparison charts for each metric
Automated rollback trigger when ensemble degradation score exceeds configured threshold for 3 consecutive probe windows
End-to-end demo: run a staged upgrade in staging vpc with probes detecting a synthetic token-throughput regression and initiating rollback

suggested_runbook: If probe ensemble triggers rollback: 1) Pause rollout and mark candidate unhealthy. 2) Collect probe traces and attach probe_seed to incident. 3) Re-run probes with reduced burst and increased sampling to confirm. 4) If confirmed, revert to previous version and open postmortem linking probe metrics. Use playbook section 'vpc-probes -> triage' in Confluence.
implementation_notes: Keep probe containers small and immutable; prefer busybox + native binary.
Label all metrics with rollout_id and probe_version for easy diffing.
Expose a probe dry-run mode that records metrics without affecting routing or capacity throttles.
Ensure probe IAM roles are least-privileged and audited by security before enabling in prod.
